newsitem.title: USA: Macerich units buy Utah's South Towne Center.
newsitem.headline: Macerich units buy Utah's South Towne Center.

text.p: Macerich Co said on Thursday it had acquired South Towne Center, a one million square foot regional mail and contiguous power center located in Sandy, Utah, for about $98 million.
The purchase price included the assumption of existing debt on the property totaling $47 million, it said. The balance of $51 million was paid in cash, Macerich said.
Macerich said it bought the property from the Zell/Merrill Lynch Real Estate Opportunity Partners I fund.

The debt assumed on the acquisitions bears interest at a rate of LIBOR plus 1.75 percent. Stabilised net operating income at the time of acquisition, on an annualised basis, was about $8.4 million, the company said.

Arthur Coppola, Macerich president, said: "This is an outstanding growth opportunity in one of the top growth markets in the United States. The South Towne Center retail complex is already a dominant force in the greater Salt Lake City marketplace."
A new 212,000 square foot Dillard's Department Store was under construction at the mall and was expected to open in September, the company said.

Macerich said it was also building 27,000 square feet of two-level mall space connecting Dillard's to the existing regional mall. The total complex would then have about 1.23 million square feet, anchored by J.C. Penney, Mervyn's and Dillard's, it said.
